episodes.205510: A severe thunderstorm tracked southeastward across Phillips County producing hail as large as 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.205668: A line of showers and isolated thunder moved through Carbon County during the afternoon of September 10th. A weak thunderstorms produced a gust of 68 mph in one of the wind prone corridors along Interstate 80.
episodes.205699: A weather system moving into the region produced thunderstorms with heavy rain over portions of interior northern California.
episodes.206235: Considerable instability, anomalously high moisture content, and a weak disturbance led to several rounds of thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.207120: On the evening of September 9th, a very subtle upper level system passed over the region, which allowed several thunderstorms to develop across the western to central Texas Panhandle. The atmosphere was strongly unstable for September standards, combined with moderate wind shear and high moisture content, and this proved to be conducive for storms to produce severe hail, winds, and localized flooding. A few severe wind gusts were observed with two of the strongest storms, the highest of which were 70 mph occurring at the NWS Amarillo office and another northeast of Palo Duro Canyon in Armstrong County. Most hail was sub-severe, but quarter sized hail was observed with a severe storm in Carson County.
episodes.207325: Thunderstorm activity spread east into Northwest Kansas from Colorado.  Hail up to tennis ball size was reported near Sharon Springs.  Dust storm conditions near Sharon Springs were associated with one of the thunderstorms.  Winds up to 75 MPH were reported, with the highest reported gust north-northwest of Ruleton.||Prolonged heavy rainfall during the night caused flooding to occur north-northeast of Tribune.  The three to four inches of rainfall caused a normally dry draw to be flooding over a road roughly 18 hours after the heavy rain had ended.
episodes.207409: An upper-level shortwave impulse helped generate a MCS that had the support of the low-level jet. While starting sub-severe, a marginal cold pool set up and generated a few severe wind gust reports.
episodes.207504: Moisture moving in from the southwest and a passing shortwave brought thunderstorms to portions of Wyoming. One thunderstorm between Meeteetse and Cody produced a 60 mph wind gust at the Dry Creek RAWS site.
episodes.207572: Tropical moisture associated with a tropical wave and other trade wind perturbations, along with an upper-level trough resulted in the formation of strong showers and thunderstorms. These showers resulted in flooding, landslide and wind damage along portions of eastern, northern and western Puerto Rico.
episodes.207715: Northwest flow over the region allowed for strong to severe storms to develop across the plains, some of which produced large hail.

events.narrative: Hail up to 1.75 inches was measured in north central Baca County.
Multiple reports of a wall of dust associated with thunderstorm winds dropping the visibility to below a quarter mile.
Half dollar to ping pong ball size hail reported in town.
Penny to tennis ball size hail fell.  Tennis ball size occurred first.
Highway 207 between Conway and Claude was closed due to three feet of water over the  highway.
Stonyford RAWS measured 3.08 inches of heavy rain in 5 hours near a strong thunderstorm.
Impassable road due to flooding at PR-2 between km 52.0 and 52.4 from Manati to Barceloneta. Two lanes were closed.
Measured from the mesonet site named KKSTRIBU27.
Mesonet station DW5288 Kendall recorded a 64 mph wind gust.
AWOS station K3K3 Syracuse recorded a 69 mph wind gust.
AWOS station K19S 1 NE Sublette reported a wind gust of 59 mph.
Public photos of running water over County Road 17, just south of County Road L.  This was 18 hours after the heavy rain had ended.
WYDOT sensor near Arlington along Interstate 80.
Panther Springs RAWS measured 1.16 inches of heavy rain in 5 hours, and 0.67 inches of heavy rain in 1 hour with strong thunderstorms over the Tehama portion of the Park Fire burn scar.
Thunderstorm outflow winds marched northward through the Bitterroot Valley, resulting in about 20 utility customers losing power. General gusts were 35 to 45 mph topping out near 50 mph.
